steps.say: We want the first two scores added: 4 + 7 = 11.
Inside the call, scores is [4, 7, 9] and k is 2.
range(1, 2) holds just one number: 1. Index 0, the first score, is skipped.
steps.error_label: Bug: the range starts at 1, but the first item is at index 0. Use range(k).

steps.say: answer is 7, not 11. With range(k) the loop visits 0 and 1 and the total is 11.

pages.title: Count the fence posts
paragraphs: range(a, b) starts at a and stops just before b, so it holds b - a numbers. range(1, 5) is 1, 2, 3, 4.
An off-by-one error is a loop that runs one time too many or too few. Write out the first and the last value before you trust a range.

key_term.definition: a loop or index that is one step too many or too few.

pages.title: First and last index
paragraphs: Python counts positions from 0. A list with 3 items has indexes 0, 1 and 2.
The last item is at len(items) - 1. items[len(items)] is one past the end and raises IndexError.

key_term.definition: the position of an item in a list, counted from 0.

transcript: Off-by-one errors are the most common bug in loops.
range starts at its first number and stops just before its second.
So range of one to five gives you one, two, three and four, but not five.
Lists count from zero, so the last item sits at length minus one.
Before you trust a loop, say its first and last value out loud.
If either one is off by a single step, you have found the bug.
